title: Association of PLA2R1 and HLA-DQA1 Polymorphisms with Risk of PLA2R-Associated Idiopathic Membranous Nephropathy in Thai Patients
content: Background and Objectives: Polymorphisms in the M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R1) and human leukocyte antigen class II alpha chain (HLA-DQA1) genes are major genetic determinants of idiopathic membranous nephropathy (iMN), yet data from Southeast Asian populations remain scarce. This study investigated the associations of PLA2R1 rs35771982 and HLA-DQA1 rs2187668 with susceptibility to PLA2R-associated iMN, their combined effects, and clinical outcomes in Thai patients. Methods: We conducted a case–control study comprising 35 patients with biopsy-proven, PLA2R-associated iMN and 108 healthy controls. Genotyping was performed via polymerase chain reaction followed by denaturing high-performance liquid chromatography. Baseline clinical parameters and 1-year treatment responses were evaluated across genotypes. Results: The PLA2R1 rs35771982 G allele (87.1% vs. 64.8%; odds ratio [OR] = 3.68, p < 0.001) and homozygous GG genotype (77.1% vs. 40.7%; recessive OR = 4.91, p < 0.001) were strongly associated with increased disease risk. Although HLA-DQA1 rs2187668 alone did not reach statistical significance (A allele: 11.4% vs. 5.1%; OR = 2.40, p = 0.064), individuals co-inheriting risk genotypes at both loci (PLA2R1 GG + HLA-DQA1 GA/AA) exhibited an 8.57-fold increased risk compared with those lacking risk alleles (OR = 8.57, p = 0.003). Neither variant significantly influenced 1-year clinical remission. Conclusions: PLA2R1 rs35771982 is a major susceptibility locus for PLA2R-associated iMN in Thai patients and co-inheritance with HLA-DQA1 rs2187668 risk genotypes was associated with the highest risk.
